sections.h2: Can I sell my house fast in Pflugerville, TX?
sections.html:
Yes. Pflugerville owners can sell for cash, list with an agent, or sell as-is, and the best route depends on the house's condition and your deadline. The city sits about fifteen miles north of Austin, so buyers here often compare it with Austin and Round Rock prices.

A cash sale trades some price for speed, fewer showings and a closing date you pick. A listing can bring a higher price but adds repairs, staging and a buyer's loan contingency. Weigh both with a written offer in hand.

  • Choose a direct sale when time, repairs, tenants or a lien make a listing hard.
  • Choose a listing when the house is in good shape and you can wait for the best price.
  • Get any offer in writing and read every closing cost line before you sign.

sections.h2: How did Pflugerville grow, and why does it matter for sellers?
sections.html:
Pflugerville is on Farm Road 1825 in northeastern Travis County. The Texas State Historical Association says it was named for Henry Pfluger, who brought his family from Germany in 1849, and that a school opened in 1872 and a Lutheran church in 1875.

The town stayed small for a long time. Its population fell to 380 by 1949, began to rise in the 1960s when it was incorporated, and reached 662 by 1980. From 1980 through 1988 it was the fastest-growing community in Texas, and the count reached 16,335 by 2000.

That fast, recent growth means many Pflugerville houses were built in waves of new subdivisions over the last few decades, not in one era. A buyer will compare your house with others of the same vintage, so builder, age and lot all matter more than street name.

sections.h2: How do Travis County property taxes work when I sell in Pflugerville?
sections.html:
Texas has no state property tax, so the bill comes from local taxing units such as the county, school district and city. The Comptroller says the appraisal district values property as of January 1 and that the tax lien attaches that same day.

Bills go out around October 1 and are delinquent after January 31. A six percent penalty and one percent interest are added on February 1, and a collection attorney can add up to 20 percent more. Appraisal notices for single-family homesteads are mailed around April 1, and most protests are due by May 15 or 30 days after notice, whichever is later.

  • School homestead exemption: $140,000 on a principal residence.
  • Age 65 or older or disabled: an added $60,000 and a school tax ceiling.
  • Appraisal cap: a homestead's appraised value cannot rise more than 10% a year.

Ask the Travis County tax office for a payoff figure, and have the title company split the current year's tax between you and the buyer at closing.

sections.h2: What are the deed and recording steps in Pflugerville?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded in the county where the land lies. For a Pflugerville house in Travis County, that means the Travis County Clerk, and the deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer.

The state county clerk manual lists $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each extra page, plus records management, archive and technology fees. Your title company will confirm the total. A general warranty or special warranty deed is common in a standard sale.

If your house straddles another county or you are unsure which county your parcel is in, ask the county appraisal district or your title company before preparing the deed. The Texas rule is that deed records go in the county where the real property is located.

sections.h2: What if my Pflugerville house has foreclosure, probate or tax problems?
sections.html:
Each has a short clock. In Texas, a lender who uses a power of sale gives a notice of default, and you can reinstate by paying the past-due amount within 20 days of the notice. A notice of sale follows at least 21 days before an auction on the first Tuesday of a month.

After a foreclosure, the lender has two years to file a deficiency suit, and surplus funds go to junior lienholders and then to the former owner. For inherited homes, a will can generally be probated within four years of death, and the owner of a homestead passing to a spouse or minor children may be able to use a small estate affidavit if the estate is $75,000 or less.

  • Missed payments: ask the servicer for a reinstatement figure in writing.
  • Back taxes: ask about installment plans, which some collectors offer for up to 36 months on a residence homestead.
  • Inherited house: confirm who has authority to sign before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: How do I compare offers on a Pflugerville house?
sections.html:
Compare the money you will actually receive and the date you will receive it. Take each offer's price, subtract commissions, repairs, carrying costs, seller concessions and title charges, and compare the results side by side.

Ask whether the buyer will close on your date, whether an inspection can cancel the deal, who pays the title policy, and whether there is an earnest money deposit. A buyer who answers in writing is easier to rely on than one who answers by phone. If you hold an HOA account, ask for a payoff or status letter early so it does not delay closing.

faqs.q: Which county records a Pflugerville deed?
faqs.a: Travis County, for a property in northeastern Travis County where Pflugerville sits. Texas deeds are filed in the county where the real property is located. Confirm your parcel's county with the title company.

faqs.q: When did Pflugerville start growing quickly?
faqs.a: In the 1980s. The Handbook of Texas says it was the fastest-growing community in the state from 1980 through 1988, and its population reached 16,335 by 2000.

faqs.q: When are Pflugerville property taxes delinquent?
faqs.a: After January 31. A six percent penalty and one percent interest are added on February 1 under the Comptroller's rules, and the penalty continues to grow monthly until July 1.

faqs.q: How long do I have to protest my appraisal before selling?
faqs.a: Most protests are due by May 15, or 30 days after the notice is delivered if that is later. The appraisal reflects value as of January 1, which can affect the tax proration at closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Pflugerville house that is behind on the mortgage?
faqs.a: Yes. The loan payoff is paid from your proceeds at closing. If a foreclosure notice has gone out, ask the servicer for the reinstatement amount and the sale date, which falls on a first Tuesday.
